Refuse. No ticket size is sane here.

The brief flags several disqualifiers. The class is OPERATOR, but the profile looks like a bundled launch: bundle_share and top3_share at 1.0, top-5 buyer share at 0.9999, sell-to-buy ratio near zero in the first two minutes after graduation (1,893 SOL bought from 7 wallets), plus a launch bot present. That is concentrated supply controlled by a few wallets, so the operator can exit at will. Recent flow is net negative for buyers, with sell SOL of 8.88 against buy SOL of 10.27 and a 30-minute high already offset by drawdown. Market cap of $27M on a $2,318 15-minute volume is wildly disconnected from liquidity, and the pool is thin relative to the claimed valuation.

Our $20 ticket would also be swamped by 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs against a stop of 20-50%, leaving no edge. Skip.
memos.scout:
The case for buying WAIF is weak, and I can't make a strong honest argument for it.

The strongest data point is the last 15 minutes: 42 buyers and 10.3 SOL of buy flow against 8.9 SOL sold, with a net inflow of 1.4 SOL and a flat return. That is fresh participation, not a collapse. The coin is alive, sitting 0.01% off its 30-minute high, and up 5.3% over 30 minutes.

But the structure undercuts it. The first two minutes after graduation show 1,893 SOL of buying from just 7 wallets, with the top 5 buyers taking nearly all of it, and bundled buyers hold the entire curve. That is the operator pattern, and its exits are controlled by the same few holders. Recent operator-backed coins have been roughly break-even, and this one is far larger than typical: a $27M market cap, with a single operator sitting on most of the supply. A 15-minute buy-to-sell ratio near 1.15 gives no assurance that the operator won't be the seller when the next wave arrives. The name "World AI Fund" is a generic hype label and adds nothing.

Against a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a base rate that favors sellers, I'd recommend skipping this one.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: insider distribution. The operator class holds the supply, and the first two minutes show 1,893 SOL bought by 7 wallets, with top-5 buyer share at 0.9999 and a launch bot present. Bundle share is 1.0 and top-3 share is 1.0, so the operator controls essentially the whole float. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes is 0.0001, but in the last 15 minutes sellers (28) already outnumber what the flow suggests, and net flow is only +1.39 SOL against 8.88 SOL sold. The 30-minute return of +5.3% is thin against a 1.4-5.1% round trip, so even a modest operator unwind erases any gain. Market cap of $27M on a 30-minute-old coin with 7 real buyers looks inflated. Skip.
